_doc: Ties of NPS Record of Treatment figures to catalogued Library of Congress records. A tie is written only after the figure image and the Library image were both looked at (confirmed_by_looking) and the feature matching (match_third_pass.py -> nps_figures_to_loc.json) gave at least 45 inliers and the record is the best candidate; the geometry of the match (tie_geometry.py: same plate, or only the same scene) is read beside it; confirm_ties.py writes this file from the hand-written decision table confirm_ties_table.py.

NF-V1-p058-000.ident: image match: the figure image (extracted from the PDF, inverted to positive) matches LOC resource cwpb.00846 (record 2018670660) with 774 inliers of 781 good matches (best other record: 8; nps_figures_to_loc.json); geometry (tie_geometry.py): SAME_PLATE, inlier fraction 0.985, scale 0.779, median residual 0.35 px; both images were looked at side by side and show the same scene
NF-V1-p058-000.note: the whole plate: a burial trench with grave boards and a wagon train beyond; the same exposure sits behind five images of the record (cwpb.00843 to 00847 match with 774, 746, 548, 440 and 214 inliers)

NF-V1-p125-000.ident: image match: the figure image (extracted from the PDF, inverted to positive) matches LOC resource ppmsca.32853 (record 2012647719) with 503 inliers of 510 good matches (best other record: 7; nps_figures_to_loc.json); the same exposure is held as record 2012647706 (resource ppmsca.32840, 424 inliers); geometry (tie_geometry.py): SAME_SCENE, inlier fraction 0.99, scale 0.83, median residual 0.43 px, failed rotation; both images were looked at side by side and show the same scene
NF-V1-p125-000.note: two men standing in a field in front of a wood: the same photograph as ppmsca.32840 (record 2012647706; 424 inliers); both records match the same Metropolitan Museum print (MET268203) with a median residual under 1 px. The rule class of tie_geometry.py is SAME_SCENE only because the figure is turned 4.2 degrees against the bar of 4.0 degrees (inlier fraction 0.99, median residual 0.4 px); called the same photograph by looking and by the 0.99 inlier fraction and the 0.4 px residual, which another exposure would not give (the turn is a difference between the two scans, not of the scene)
